notes: The participant landing page opens directly to the consent form, which is displayed in a compact scrollable reader before study credentials are created.

After consent, students choose a non-identifying Participant ID; the server generates a one-time-display Private Access Key and stores only its hash. Python/Java is selected once after access creation and before the pre-survey.
Pre/post survey item structure is preserved while Python/Java wording follows the selected language.
Practice uses an assigned 2/1/1 sequence for four questions total, with later modalities locked until prior completion.
Problem Solving and Debugging use sandbox Run Code and visible scoring; Code Explanation has a read-only code view and explanation scoring with no Run Code.
Participant-facing session labels do not advertise specific programming topics.
Dedicated survey exports, live-release readiness controls, and duplicate-entry protection are available in the research dashboard.
Question definitions are versioned by bank hash so future edits do not silently alter already-started sessions.
Heartbeat/database chatter, shared-campus IP limits, external-provider bursts, and score JSON reliability were hardened for large scheduled cohorts.

Remote self-enrollment now opens when deliveryMode is remote, LIVE_COLLECTION_ENABLED is true, and deployment startup checks pass; participant consent, ID validation, rate limiting, duplicate protection, and hashed access-key storage remain enforced.
deploymentFixes: Fixed stale unparenthesized CASE expression in migrations/002_workflow.sql.
Regenerated supabase_upgrade.sql, supabase_workflow.sql, and supabase_setup.sql from the corrected source migration.
Added migration consistency checks to npm run check.
Changed Render liveness health check to /healthz so database migration problems do not fail the web-service deployment.
Removed mandatory Supabase RPC call before the HTTP server starts; study configuration now initializes lazily.
Added /health setup diagnostics and /readyz strict readiness diagnostics.
Database configuration errors now produce actionable 503 messages rather than crashing the Node process.
scoring: OpenAI rubric scoring for problem-solving, debugging, and code-explanation; sandbox evidence is supplied for runnable modalities.
releaseHash: Includes consent, surveys, assessments, input schemas, current question bank, and study design config (excluding release metadata and session open/closed switches).
